messages:
nora: FYI we started seeing SCIM deprovisioning fail for a customer (acct-778) — their OIDC id_tokens are being rejected by our validator. Errors show `aud mismatch` and downstream RBAC-change webhooks are returning 403.

diego: can you paste the exact error and an example token header/payload?

nora: error from oauth-validate: `invalid_claim: aud claim mismatch (expected string 'redwood-api', got ['redwood-api','client-portal']) user=acct-778`. example payload (redacted): `{
  \"iss\": \"https://idp.customer.example\",\n  \"sub\": \"user-abc\",\n  \"aud\": [\"redwood-api\", \"client-portal\"],\n  \"exp\": 1710000000
}``

leah: interesting — spec allows aud to be string or array. our validator expects a string only. vendor probably started including the portal audience. that would break our aud equality check.

own: consequences: SCIM deprov + RBAC webhook calls are authenticated with id_token and we gate by audience. so tokens validate -> allowed. now they reject -> we deny and create audit entries `rbac:deny 403`.

security-bot: ALERT: spike in `invalid_claim: aud` errors for tenant acct-778 @10:14 local — rate 45/min.

diego: immediate mitigations?

nora: short fix: accept aud arrays and treat token valid if expected audience is present. We should be cautious: if aud contains unexpected entries we still validate exp/iss/signature.

leah: agree. patch suggestion (pseudo-js):
```js
const aud = payload.aud;
if (Array.isArray(aud)) {
  if (!aud.includes(EXPECTED_AUD)) throw new InvalidClaim('aud');
} else if (aud !== EXPECTED_AUD) {
  throw new InvalidClaim('aud');
}
```
This keeps strictness but supports arrays.

own: quick question re: KMS — any key wrapping or envelope encryption involved here? could KMS rotation cause different aud?

diego: no, KMS only used for our signing keys for service tokens. This is IdP-side change to audiences. But we should check KMS audit just in case. I ran a query: no KMS rekeys in timeframe.

eng-oncall: INCIDENT CREATED #inc-2026-058-aud-array-deprov-fail severity:P3 owners:@nora @diego runbook: identity/aud-claims.md

nora: timeline: 10:12 first failure, 10:14 spike after vendor deploy of portal feature that added extra aud, 10:17 we deployed validator patch to canary, 10:20 canary green, 10:22 promoted. errors dropped to baseline by 10:25.

leah: follow-ups: 1) add unit test for aud string/array; 2) add a compatibility test in CI that fetches example id_tokens from vendor testbed (if available); 3) add telemetry to tag `aud_form` (string|array) per tenant; 4) update onboarding docs to list aud contract expectations.

security-bot: NOTE: auditing change requested 1: map existing `rbac:deny` entries for acct-778 to a new audit code `IDP_AUD_ARRAY` to distinguish validation rejections from policy denies.

own: can we retroactively annotate the failed RBAC entries so customers see the real cause in the audit UI?

diego: yes, we can map by trace id and annotate. nora, please export trace ids for the window 10:12-10:26 and we'll bulk-update audit entries with `IDP_AUD_ARRAY`.

nora: done, exported and attached to incident doc. also emailed vendor SRE to suggest they avoid adding audiences without coordination.

leah: one security note: accepting aud arrays widens token semantics slightly. we must ensure we only accept arrays that include our expected aud and still reject tokens with malicious audience sets. Add a unit test where aud array contains similar-but-not-equal strings.

own: add a runtime guard: if aud array length > 5 consider rate-limit/alert (anomalous token).

nora: postmortem items: root cause (vendor added additional audience claim array), mitigation (validator patch to accept aud arrays if expected aud present), long term (CI compatibility tests + onboarding contract + telemetry + audit code), severity P3.

diego: I'll open the PR and include tests + changelog note. target rolling deploy to canary then 10% then global.

security-bot: REMINDER: update compliance ticket with annotated audit entries and include the mapped trace IDs.

nora: thanks, closing once compliance confirms audit annotations are visible to customer compliance rep. :white_check_mark:
